title: Once Upon a Time in America
events_chronological: In 1918 on the Lower East Side, young Noodles and his friends Patsy, Cockeye and Dominic run errands and petty rackets for the local boss Bugsy.
Max arrives in the neighbourhood, and after fighting each other the two boys join forces.
Noodles watches Deborah dance alone through a peephole in the back of her father's delicatessen.
The boys start robbing drunks and hide their money in a suitcase in a railway station locker.
Bugsy shoots Dominic dead in the street, Noodles knifes Bugsy in return, and Noodles is sent to prison.
Released in 1930, Noodles finds Max running a large Prohibition operation with Patsy and Cockeye.
The gang work for the union organiser Jimmy O'Donnell and the crooked police chief Aiello, whose newborn son they swap in the maternity ward.
Noodles hires a deserted seafront restaurant for a night with Deborah, and rapes her in the car when she tells him she is leaving for Hollywood.
Prohibition ends, and Max, unwilling to stop, proposes robbing the Federal Reserve.
Carol and Noodles agree that the only way to save Max from himself is to have him arrested on a smaller job.
Noodles telephones the police to tip them off, and is told at the scene that Max, Patsy and Cockeye were shot dead and their bodies burned in the street.
Noodles goes to the station locker for the gang's money, finds the suitcase empty, and leaves New York under another name.
In an opium den in 1933, Noodles lies back and smiles at the ceiling.
In 1968 Noodles receives an invitation to the reinterment of his three friends in a mausoleum he never paid for.
Noodles comes back to New York, finds Fat Moe still behind the delicatessen counter, and is given the key to the same locker.
Noodles finds the mausoleum with his own name on the plaque and a suitcase of money inside, described as an advance on his next job.
Noodles visits an aged Carol at the Bailey Foundation retirement home, and she tells him Max had wanted to die.
Noodles finds Deborah backstage, now Secretary Bailey's mistress, and she tries to send him away without letting him see her son.
Noodles goes to Secretary Bailey's house and finds Max alive, having stolen everything, now asking Noodles to kill him.
Noodles refuses to recognise him and walks away, and a garbage truck grinds past behind him as Max disappears.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts between three eras - 1918-22, 1930-33 and 1968 - without captions, carrying each jump on a sound or an object: a telephone that will not stop ringing, a Frisbee, a shot through a peephole. It opens in 1933 at told-order bullets 1-3, jumps thirty-five years forward at bullet 4, then fifty years back at bullet 6, and thereafter alternates, so a childhood scene and an old man's return repeatedly sit side by side.
fabula_notes: The 1968 frame may be an opium dream Noodles is having in 1933 - the closing smile invites the reading and the film never settles it - and the ordering here takes the three eras as literally successive. The thirty-five years Noodles spends hiding in Buffalo are elided entirely, and Max's survival is explained only in retrospect.
